id1.description: The local measurement of arterial blood pressure which is a surrogate for arterial. pressure in the systemic circulation.  Most commonly, use of the term 'blood pressure' refers to measurement of brachial artery pressure in the upper arm.

at5.description: Peak systemic arterial blood pressure  - measured in systolic or contraction phase of the heart cycle.

at6.description: Minimum systemic arterial blood pressure - measured in the diastolic or relaxation phase of the heart cycle.

id9.description: The position of the subject at the time of measurement.

id14.description: The size of the cuff used for blood pressure measurement.

id15.description: Common body sites where blood pressure is recorded.

at16.description: A cuff used for an adult thigh - bladder approx 20cm x 42cm.

at17.description: A cuff for adults with larger arms - bladder approx 16cm x 38cm.

at18.description: A cuff that is standard for an adult - bladder approx 13cm x 30cm.

at26.description: The right arm of the person.

at27.description: The left arm of the person.

at28.description: The right thigh of the person.

at29.description: The left thigh of the person.

at1001.description: Standing at the time of blood pressure measurement.

at1002.description: Sitting (for example on bed or chair) at the time of blood pressure measurement.

at1003.description: Reclining at the time of blood pressure measurement.

at1004.description: Lying flat at the time of blood pressure measurement.

at1006.description: The craniocaudal tilt of the surface on which the person is lying at the time of measurement.

at1007.description: The average arterial pressure that occurs over the entire course of the heart contraction and relaxation cycle.

at1008.description: The difference between the systolic and diastolic pressure.

at1009.description: A cuff used for a small adult - bladder approx 10cm x 24cm.

at1010.description: A cuff that is appropriate for a child or adult with a thin arm - bladder approx 8cm x 21cm.

id1011.description: Record which Korotkoff sound is used for determining diastolic pressure using auscultative method.

at1012.description: The fourth Korotkoff sound is identified as an abrupt muffling of sounds.

at1013.description: The fifth Korotkoff sound is identified by absence of sounds as the cuff pressure drops below the diastolic blood pressure.

at1015.description: Lying flat with some lateral tilt, usually angled towards the left side.   Commonly required in the last trimester of pregnancy to relieve aortocaval compression.

at1019.description: A cuff used for infants - bladder approx 5cm x 15cm.

at1020.description: A cuff used for a neonate, assuming cuff is the appropriate size for maturity and birthweight of the neonate.

at1021.description: The right wrist of the subject.

at1022.description: The left wrist of the subject.

at1026.description: Details about sphygmomanometer or other device used to measure the blood pressure.

at1027.description: The right ankle of the subject.

at1031.description: Details about physical activity undertaken at the time of blood pressure.measurement.

at1032.description: The left ankle of the subject.

at1033.description: A finger of the subject.  Identification of the finger can be recorded in 'Specific Location' data element, if required.

id1034.description: Body location where blood pressure is measured.  Use 'Location of measurement' to select from common sites.  Use 'Specific location' to record more specific details or a site that is not in the common set or to refer to an external terminology.

id1035.description: Specific details about the body site where blood pressure is recorded.

id1036.description: Method of measurement of blood pressure.

at1037.description: Method of measuring blood pressure externally, using a stethoscope and Korotkoff sounds.

at1038.description: Method of measuring blood pressure externally, using palpation (usually of the brachial or radial arteries).

id1039.description: Formula used to calculate the MAP (if recorded in data).

at1040.description: Method of measuring blood pressure externally, using a blood pressure machine.

at1041.description: Method of measuring blood pressure internally ie involving penetration of the skin and measuring inside blood vessels.

at1043.description: Estimate of the average blood pressure over a 24 hour period.

id1044.description: Sleep status - supports interpretation of 24 hour ambulatory blood pressure records.

at1046.description: Subject is in the natural state of bodily rest.

at1052.description: A toe of the subject.   Identification of the toe can be recorded in 'Specific Location' data element, if required.

at1053.description: Comment on and record other incidental factors that may be contributing to the blood pressure measurement.  For example, level of anxiety or 'white coat syndrome'; pain or fever; changes in atmospheric pressure etc.

at1054.description: Invasive measurement via transducer access line within an artery. Location of the transducer can be recorded in 'Specific Location' data element, if required.

ac1.description: The position of the subject at the time of measurement.

ac2.description: Sleep status - supports interpretation of 24 hour ambulatory blood pressure records.

ac3.description: The size of the cuff used for blood pressure measurement.

ac4.description: Common body sites where blood pressure is recorded.

ac5.description: Method of measurement of blood pressure.

ac6.description: Record which Korotkoff sound is used for determining diastolic pressure using auscultative method.
